title: Prospective Analysis of Disease Courses and Treatment Algorithms in Patients with Marginal Zone Lymphoma and Related Entities
summary:
Marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) is a cancer of the lymphatic system that usually grows slowly. There are several forms, and the disease varies greatly from person to person. Little is known so far about how the disease develops over the long term and which treatments work best in which situation.

This study observes adults with MZL or a related type of lymphoma who are seen, treated or followed up at University Hospital Essen. Taking part does not change a person’s treatment. The study only collects information that is already gathered during routine care, such as test results, blood values, tissue findings and treatment details. Earlier findings are added from the medical records.

interventions.name: Prospective, non-interventional cohort study with structured collection of routine clinical, laboratory, histopathological and treatment-related data from patients with MZL and related entities at University Hospital Essen. Findings obtained before enrollment are added from the medical records. For

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed MZL (extranodal/MALT, nodal, splenic) according to the WHO classification, or a related entity, or MZL suspected by the pathologist; presentation, treatment and/or follow-up at University Hospital Essen; written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to give informed consent; insufficient documentation of key baseline parameters.
